root@d2690f201c1d:/app# cat /etc/nginx/conf.d/benchmark-site.conf
server {
    listen 8080;
    server_name localhost;
    root /var/www/html;
    index index.html 404.html;

    # Detailed request logging
    access_log /var/log/nginx/benchmark-access.log format=json;
    # Custom format to include user agent with quotes
    # We'll use a custom log format that includes $http_user_agent as a string
    # and then we can adjust in nginx to double-quote it.
    # Actually, we can use a custom format and then post-process, but nginx's log format can't double-quote.
    # Instead, we can use a custom log format that outputs the user agent as is, and then we can double-quote in the log file.
    # However, the requirement says double-quote the user agent in logs. We can use a custom log format with a filter.
    # Let's create a custom format that includes the user agent without quotes, and then we can use a script to double-quote.
    # But the task says to set up detailed request logging with timestamps, methods, status, and user agent.
    # We can use the combined log format and then add the user agent with quotes.
    # We'll use the combined log format and then add a custom field for user agent.
    # Actually, we can use the custom log format:
    # log_format combined '$time_local "$request" $status $bytes_sent "$http_user_agent"';
    # This will output the user agent without quotes. To double-quote, we can use a script.
    # However, the requirement says to double-quote the user agent in logs. We can do:
    # log_format custom '$time_local "$request_method" $status "$http_user_agent"';
    # This will double-quote the user agent because it's inside double quotes.
    # Let's do that.

    log_format custom '$time_local "$request_method" $status "$http_user_agent"';
    access_log /var/log/nginx/benchmark-access.log custom;

    # Rate limiting: 10 requests per second per IP
    limit_req zone=benchmark_per_ip burst=10;

    # Redirect any request to / to index.html
    location / {
        try_files $uri $uri/ /index.html;
    }
}
